\U0001F1F2\U0001F1FD\U0001F3ED <u>MEXICO BACK IN THE GLOBAL TOP 10 FOR FOREIGN INVESTMENT — $41 BILLION IN 2025</u>

Mexico pulled in $41 billion in foreign direct investment in 2025, up from $38 billion in 2024, climbing from 11th to 10th worldwide and holding 2nd in Latin America behind Brazil, per UN data. It is the first time Mexico has cracked the global top 10 since 2021 — Hacienda says it “reflects confidence.” So much for the instability the business press keeps forecasting under the 4T.

\U0001F1F2\U0001F1FD\U0001F49C <u>MEXICO CITY MAKES CARE A RIGHT — FIRST LAW TO VALUE UNPAID DOMESTIC WORK</u>

Clara Brugada promulgated Mexico City’s new Care System Law — the first to officially measure and put an economic value on unpaid domestic work, and to treat caregiving as a shared social responsibility rather than women’s invisible duty. Delivered through the Utopías and new “Houses of the Three Rs,” Brugada calls it “the construction of a welfare state with a feminist perspective.”

\U0001F1F2\U0001F1FD\U0001F6E2️ <u>MEXICO WON’T FRACK ON FAITH — SCIENTISTS SAY THE CLEAN-TECH CASE ISN’T PROVEN</u>

A commission of 17 researchers from UNAM, UAM, the National Polytechnic and the Mexican Petroleum Institute told the Sheinbaum government its assessment of “cleaner” fracking is not conclusive — no technology yet exists that uses less water and less contamination for Mexico’s non-conventional gas. Until the science says otherwise, there is no green light for shale extraction.

\U0001F1F2\U0001F1FD\U0001F30E <u>MEXICO MODERNIZES ITS SWISS/EFTA TRADE DEAL — DIVERSIFYING AS TRUMP RATTLES TARIFFS</u>

Sheinbaum and Swiss President Guy Parmelin agreed to modernize the 25-year-old free-trade agreement between Mexico and the EFTA bloc (Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein), with bilateral trade already at $4.272 billion in 2025. “We are both pacifist countries, convinced of the peaceful resolution of disputes,” Sheinbaum said — one more market opened as Mexico steadily diversifies away from dependence on Washington.

\U0001F6A8\U0001F1F2\U0001F1FD <u>ONE OF THE “43” WAS A SOLDIER THE ARMY PLANTED INSIDE AYOTZINAPA</u>

Alejandro Encinas, who led the Truth Commission from 2018 to 2023, confirmed the Army had infiltrated one of its own — Julio César López Patolzin — into the Ayotzinapa rural normal school under “the façade of a student,” registered as a military intelligence body. President Sheinbaum says new investigative advances are ready to present and reminds that soldiers have been prosecuted and detained in the case since the previous administration.

\U0001F1F2\U0001F1FD\U0001F1FB\U0001F1EA <u>MEXICO STANDS WITH VENEZUELA — 261 PERSONNEL, 71 TONS OF AID, AND MORE ON OFFER</u>

While Washington piles new sanctions on Caracas, Mexico sent 261 rescue and medical personnel — 240 Army, 11 Air Force, 10 National Guard — plus over 71 tons of food and medicine after twin quakes (M7.5 and M7.2) killed 4,490 people and left 17,907 homeless. Today Sheinbaum said Mexico is ready to send more the moment Venezuela requests it: “México es solidario.”

BLOOMBERG: Mexico, Peru Open Door To Restoring Relations After Bitter Political Fight
July 10, 2026 | 🟡

Bloomberg: Mexico & Peru "open door" to restoring ties — quietly framing the "bitter fight" as Mexico's doing for granting asylum. Left soft-focus: Peru cut ties because Mexico called the jailing of Pedro Castillo's family what it was.

Mexico's "interference" was giving asylum to a deposed president's wife and children; Boluarte's post-coup crackdown that killed dozens of protesters goes unmentioned.

• "We are going to wait." — Sheinbaum on Fujimori
• Peru severed ties because Mexico "maintained the former president was being held illegally"

CNN: After a year of tariffs, automakers are still resistant to moving production to the US
July 12, 2026 | 🟢

CNN, one year into Trump's auto tariffs: carmakers "would rather pay the tariffs" than leave Mexico. Toyota's own words — its US investments are "multi-decade decisions," not tariff policy. The great reshoring that was promised never came.

Trump called Toyota's Tacoma move "Tariffs at work"; Toyota politely said it wasn't. Credit where due — CNN ran the numbers straight.

• "too many costs and too much uncertainty… to make widespread changes"
• "multi-decade decisions based on broader strategic goals" — Toyota

NY POST: US-born drug lord takes over Mexico's deadliest cartel — creating legal headache for Trump admin
July 11, 2026 | 🤡

NY Post: the new boss of CJNG was born in Santa Ana, California — and that's a "legal headache for Trump." A US citizen runs Mexico's deadliest cartel, and the paper still files the whole thing under Mexico's problem.

His US citizenship, the Post frets, "should protect him" from a lethal operation — a courtesy never extended to the Mexican nationals shot in ICE custody this month.

• "US-born drug lord takes over Mexico's deadliest cartel"
• his citizenship "should protect him from… an operation that would put his life in unnecessary jeopardy" — ex-US official

BBC: The Chinese graduate accused of being Mexico's 'fentanyl king'
July 13, 2026 | 🟡

BBC's deep-dive on Mexico's "fentanyl king" — a Chinese chemist-turned-broker — carefully names China's suppliers and Mexico's labs. What it never names once: US demand, or the US guns arming the cartels it spends 2,000 words describing.

A supply-side story with the buyer erased — 160,000 Chinese chemical firms get scrutiny, the largest fentanyl market on earth gets none.

• "a broker that connected Mexican organisations with Chinese suppliers of precursor chemicals" — InSight Crime
• "pumped massive quantities of cocaine, fentanyl, and methamphetamine" into the US — DOJ
